builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
summary: guardscope replaces trusting a runtime control's marketing or documentation claims about which agent action paths it inspects with a static-plus-empirical audit that reconciles the control's decision records against kernel-level ground truth, classifying each action as checked, bypassed, or prevented. It costs the engineering effort to instrument deployments with kernel-level tracing, run the fixed workload across one of eight topology designs, and integrate the framework into your agent harness, plus the latency inherent in any runtime control you choose to verify. It can fail if your production topology differs from the tested designs, if kernel-level instrumentation is unavailable or restricted in your environment (e.g., managed containers), or if a control's coverage holds under the fixed workload but breaks under your actual traffic patterns.
rationale: For a small team deploying LLM agents behind gateways or governance toolkits, this framework is directly adoptable at small scale to verify that a chosen runtime control actually sees the actions it claims to check, but its value depends on the team's specific topology and harness, so workload-specific validation is required before relying on it in production.
technique: Kernel-verified coverage measurement for agent runtime controls
